body.statement: For every simple graph \(G\) on \(n\geq1\) vertices, the rational construction with \(\varepsilon_n=[2^{40}(n+1)^4]^{-1}\), \(g=\varepsilon_n^2\), \(\delta=\varepsilon_n^3\), \(p=-25/16\), and \(r=(15/16)(1-\delta)\) satisfies \(\rho(B_G)<1\) and \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{stab}}(W_G)=\{\pi_S:S\in\mathcal I(G)\}\). Every independent intended assignment obeys \(\rho(B_{\pi_S})\leq\max\{9/10,1-\delta/10\}\); every non-independent intended assignment has an eigenvalue of modulus at least \(1+g/20\); every other admissible assignment is unstable; and \(W_G\) has \(O(\log(n+1))\) bits per nonzero entry.
body.justification: The theorem turns a global spectral filter on a causal equivalence class into an exact, coefficient-valid combinatorial family with explicit margins.
body.gap: Lacerda et al. screen assignments and prove a disjoint-cycle uniqueness result; they do not realize arbitrary independent-set systems or control every unintended row permutation.
body.consumer: It supplies the missing stability-conditioned orbit oracle boundary for matching-frequency calculations in cyclic-LiNG intervention design.
body.proof_tex:
First, every intended permutation \(\pi_S\) is admissible. A fixed coordinate uses a diagonal entry equal to one, while a \(u_i\)-\(v_i\) swap uses the two nonzero entries \(W_G[v_i,u_i]=-p=25/16\) and \(W_G[u_i,v_i]=-1\). Distinct subsets give distinct permutations.

The analytic-homotopy certification theorem exhausts the spectrum of each intended assignment. If \(S\in\mathcal I(G)\), its \(3n-2|S|\) noncritical roots have modulus less than \(9/10\), and its remaining roots lie in the two critical disks and have modulus at most \(1-\delta/10\). Therefore
\[
 \rho(B_{\pi_S})\leq\max\left\{\frac9{10},1-\frac\delta{10}\right\}<1.
\]
In particular, \(S=\varnothing\) proves \(\rho(B_G)<1\). If \(S\notin\mathcal I(G)\), the same theorem supplies an eigenvalue of modulus at least \(1+g/20\), so \(\pi_S\) is not stable.

It remains only to check completeness of the orbit. The support-cycle classification in the certification theorem shows that every admissible permutation not equal to an intended \(\pi_S\) either contains a root-only cycle or contains a local \(u_i\)-\(w_i\) swap. In the first case its spectral radius is greater than \(1/(2g)>1\). In the second case, when no root-only cycle is present, it has an eigenvalue with real part greater than \(5/4\), hence with modulus greater than one. Thus every unintended admissible assignment is unstable, and
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{stab}}(W_G)
 =\{\pi_S:S\in\mathcal I(G)\}.
\]

The proposition on gadget-law validity shows simultaneously that the reference and every normalized assignment are legal same-law cyclic LiNG mechanisms; the spectral argument is therefore inside the declared causal model rather than merely matrix algebra. Finally, the only nonintegral entries are formed from
\[
 \varepsilon_n=\frac{1}{2^{40}(n+1)^4},\qquad
 g=\varepsilon_n^2,\qquad
 \delta=\varepsilon_n^3,\qquad
 p=-\frac{25}{16},\qquad
 r=\frac{15}{16}(1-\delta).
\]
Their numerators and denominators have \(O(\log(n+1))\) bits, and the adjacency entries are zero or one. Constructing the \(3n\)-dimensional sparse matrix takes polynomial time and preserves this per-entry bit bound. All assertions of the theorem follow.
